rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When istawā is joined to ilā, it means to take a straight direction or turn directly toward something.
rows.anchor: ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ kelimesi إِلَى ile sılalandığı zaman istikāmet almak, dosdoğru teveccüh etmek mânasınadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Regarding God, Elmalılı interprets the phrase as God's direct will and direction of divine care toward the heaven.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ hakkında doğrudan doğru irade ile tefsir olunur. Yani inâyet-i ilâhiyesini doğrudan semâya doğru tevcih buyurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can mean that earth and heaven submit together whether or not it suits their natures, or that they come into existence.
rows.anchor: tabiatlarınıza gerek muvâfık olsun gerek olmasın, yahut ikiniz de vücûda gelin, tekevvün edin

rows.speaker: Râzî ve Kadı Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Some commentators take thumma as rank-sequence rather than time: heaven was created before earth but described after its creation.
rows.anchor: Râzî ve Kadı Beyzâvî gibi müfessirînin bir kısmı zamânî değil, rütbî terâhî ile anlamışlar

rows.speaker: Râzî ve Kadı Beyzâvî
rows.claim: On this reading, come means come into being, and smoke describes the first, still dark primordial matter.
rows.anchor: Bu surette ٱئْتِيَا demek “vücûda gelin” mânasına tekvinden ibarettir. “Duhan” da ilk maddenin yaratıldığı hâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı calls that reading good but objects that the circumstantial clause and preceding command risk implying the primordial matter is eternal.
rows.anchor: maddenin kıdemini îhâm etmek gibi bir şâibe vardır

rows.speaker: ekser müfessirîn; author
rows.claim: Most commentators read thumma temporally: earth was first created before heaven, though its spreading came later as 79:30 states; Elmalılı prefers this majority reading.
rows.anchor: ekser müfessirîn ise ثُمَّ’nin terâhisi zamânî olduğuna kāil olmuşlar ve Arz’ın ilk halkı semâdan evvel olup ancak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes heaven here to mean the region above earth, the air, as in other verses describing rain sent down from heaven.
rows.anchor: olduğu gibi Arz’ın yukarısı, yani hava tarafı demek olduğuna zâhib oluyorum

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account earth was initially fiery as it separated from heaven, and gases rose from that fire to form the smoky upper region.
rows.anchor: Arz ilk yaratılışında ibtidâ semâdan ayrıldığı sıra ateş hâlinde idi, sonra bu ateşten onun yukarısına doğru semâsı olarak duman hâlinde gazlar püskürüyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God orders the smoky heaven and earth to move together in an ordered system, adjusting to one another whether their natures welcome it or not.
rows.anchor: kerhen gelin tabiatınıza uygun gelse de gelmese de ikiniz birlikte birbirinize uyarak bir nizam üzere hareket edin dedi

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some commentators understand the command and willing response in a conscious, sentient sense.
rows.anchor: şu‘ûrî mânada anlamak istemişlerse de mutlak tevâfuk ve inkıyad mânasına olmak daha mütebâdirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers the more immediate sense of complete concord and obedience rather than conscious speech.
rows.anchor: mutlak tevâfuk ve inkıyad mânasına olmak daha mütebâdirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created things accept even effects contrary to their ordinary nature as part of their nature, so no created thing disobeys divine command.
rows.anchor: Emr-i ilâhîye karşı hiçbir muhalefetleri vâki‘olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the receptivity called the law of inertia can explain the natural-seeming events of all celestial and terrestrial bodies.
rows.anchor: Onun için “atâlet kanunu” denilen bu mutâva‘at ve kābiliyet ile bütün ecrâm-ı semâviye ve ecsâm-ı arziyenin hâdisâtı tabî‘î imiş gibi îzah olunabilir.

rows.speaker: قِيل
rows.claim: An unattributed account says the Throne rested on water before creation; heat produced curd and smoke, the curd became earth, and the rising smoke became heaven.
rows.anchor: Denilmiş ki semâvât ve Arz halk olunmadan Arş su üzerinde idi, sudaki suhûnetten bir kaymak ve bir duman çıktı

rows.speaker: Fahr-i Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says this account is absent from the Qur'an and appears at the beginning of what Jews call the Torah; it could be accepted if evidence supported it.
rows.anchor: Fahr-i Râzî der ki: “Bu kıssa Kur’an’da yoktur, Yehûd’un Tevrat dediği kitabın evvelinde vardır. Bir delil delâlet ederse kabul olunabilir.”

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî
rows.claim: Zamakhshari also transmits an unusual account in which dry land became earth and then split into two earths.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî garib bir fıkra daha nakleder de kuraktan bir arz yaptı, sonra da onu ayırdı iki arz yaptı der

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı wonders whether Zamakhshari's two earths might mean the Moon separating from earth or the separation of America.
rows.anchor: Ayrılan bu iki arz nedir? Ya Arz’dan Kamer’in ayrılması olacak, yahut da Amerika’nın ayrılması olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reckoning makes the two days the creation of primordial matter before earth and the later formation of celestial bodies, two days within the six-day creation.
rows.anchor: ilk maddenin halkı, birisi de ecrâmın teşekkülü günleridir ki Sûre-i A‘râf’ta beyan olunduğu üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, one day precedes earth's creation and the other follows it, since bodies such as the Moon, Venus and Mercury were created afterward; this preserves the sequential sense of fa.
rows.anchor: Yahut birisi Arz’ın halkından evveli, birisi de Arz’ın halkından sonrasıdır. Çünkü Kamer, Zühre, Utarid gibi bazı ecrâmın halkı Arz’dan sonradır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As his own further possibility, Elmalılı suggests that the two days may be one of this world and one of the afterlife, treating them as future states of the heavens.
rows.anchor: üzere biri dünya biri âhiret olmak da muhtemildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also revealed to the angels of each heaven the commands governing the events that would take place there, completing its ordering.
rows.anchor: her semânın meleklerine orada cereyan edecek şuûnun emrini de telkin buyurdu ki bu da itmam cümlesindendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God adorned the lowest heaven with bright lamps and guarded it so that devils could not approach.
rows.anchor: dünyâ semâyı misbahlar, yani parlak kandillerle donattık süsledik بِزِينَةٍ ٱلْكَوَاكِبِ [es-Sâffât 37/6]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered creation is the decree of the Mighty, All-Knowing, followed by a rebuke asking whether the hearers will persist in disbelief.
rows.anchor: o, O Azîz Alîm’in takdîridir. Siz O’na hep küfür mü edip duracaksınız?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is of a severe punishment that destroys in a lightning-like stroke, like the calamities of Ad and Thamud.
rows.anchor: bir sâ‘ika tehlikesi haber veriyorum yani yıldırım gibi bir çarpışta helâk edecek şiddetli bir azab

rows.speaker: Câbir b. Abdullah
rows.claim: Jabir reports that Utba offered Muhammad leadership, wealth and wives; after the Prophet recited Fussilat through the Ad–Thamud warning, Utba stopped him and later told Quraysh the speech was neither magic, poetry nor divination, fearing punishment.
rows.anchor: Delâilü’n-Nübüvve’de Beyhakī ve İbn Asâkîr Câbir b. Abdullah’tan rivayet ederler, demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Saîd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr initially interprets the requested affection as love for the kin of Muhammad's family.
rows.anchor: Saîd b. Cübeyr “âl-i Muhammed karâbeti” deyivermiş

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Sa'id was hasty: every Quraysh clan had kinship with the Prophet, so they should at least honor their kinship with him.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki: “Acele ettin, Kureyş’ten bir batın yoktur ki Peygamber aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’a bir karâbeti bulunmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they do not honor the Prophet's rights as messenger and mercy to all worlds, they should at least respect their kinship, listen and cease hostility.
rows.anchor: Nübüvvet ve risâletim ve rahmeten li’l-âlemîn olmam haysiyetleriyle olan hukūkumu tanımıyorsanız, bari aramızdaki akrabalık hukūkuna riayet edin

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the phrase as a request to love those related to the Prophet, his own relatives.
rows.anchor: Bana karâbeti olanları, yani akrabamı sevmenizi isterim” diye mâna verenler de olmuştur

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some narrow the relatives in this interpretation specifically to the descendants of Ali and Fatima.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bu karâbeti Ali ve Fâtıma evlâdına tahsis etmek istemişlerdir

rows.speaker: Hasan; Abd b. Humeyd
rows.claim: A report from Hasan interprets the phrase as love of drawing near to God through good deeds; qurba here means nearness to God, not kinship.
rows.anchor: yakınlıkta meveddet, yani güzel amellerle Allah’a tekarrub hususunda sevgi demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers the third interpretation as more inclusive and better suited to the surrounding context, especially the following promise about earning a good deed.
rows.anchor: Ve bu mâna hem e‘amdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever earns a good deed receives a better reward; the deed's goodness increases and God grants the capacity to perform even better deeds.
rows.anchor: artmış olur, hem de daha güzelini yapmak melekesi ihsan edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghafur means that God covers or forgives sins.
rows.anchor: çünkü Allah Gafûr’dur günahları örter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shakur means that God repays good deeds with beautiful reward and never lets their recompense go to waste.
rows.anchor: Şekûr’dur güzel amellere güzel sevap ve mükafat ile mukabele eder. Hasenâtın ecrini zâyi‘etmez

words: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge is that the Prophet fabricated the Qur'an and falsely attributed it to God.
rows.anchor: Bu Kur’ân’ı yalan olarak uydurup Allah’a isnad ile iftira etti diye iftira mı ediyorlar?

words: فَإِن يَشَإِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those accusing the Prophet of lying have sealed hearts unable to hear truth; God could also seal the Prophet's heart by withdrawing revelation and grace.
rows.anchor: senin kalbinin üzerini de mühürleyiverir; vahyini, lütfunu kesiverir

words: فَإِن يَشَإِ ٱللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not grieve over their accusations but give thanks for God's favor.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde sen onların dediklerine keder etme de Allah’ın lütfuna şükret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God erases falsehood and establishes truth, so the deniers' claims fade, the Prophet's prophethood is confirmed and the Qur'an's promises come true; a false Qur'an would soon be erased.
rows.anchor: Kur’an yalan olsa idi Allah onu tahakkuk ettirmez, çok sürmeden mahvederdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the innermost thoughts in both the Prophet's heart and the accusers' hearts.
rows.anchor: senin kalbindekini de bilir, onların kalblerindekini de

words: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Therefore, the sinners should repent promptly and abandon their evil deeds.
rows.anchor: binâen‘aleyh o günahkârlar da hemen tevbe edip o seyyiâttan vazgeçmelidirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent wording indicates that living creatures exist in the heavens as well as on earth.
rows.anchor: göklerde de hayvânât vardır. Mücâhid de buna kāil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid likewise holds that there are living creatures in the heavens.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid de buna kāil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: Diğer bazıları
rows.claim: Some take the heavenly creatures to mean animals flying in the air; Elmalılı says there is no need for this interpretation.
rows.anchor: Diğer bazıları ise semâvâttaki “dâbbe”den murad havada uçuşan hayvânât olduğuna zâhib olmuşlarsa da, böyle bir tevile zarûret yoktur

words: وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ جَمْعِهِمْ إِذَا يَشَآءُ قَدِيرٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can gather all these creatures whenever He wills, so there is no reason to doubt resurrection.
rows.anchor: Onun için haşr ü neşirde tereddüde mahal yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting Pharaoh's fate, God recounts His favor to Moses and his people: drowning and destruction served to secure Israel's rescue.
rows.anchor: o gark ve tahrîbin hikmeti bu necâtı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's selection was deliberate, based on qualities and favors God had granted, and served as a test, as in 11:7 and 67:2.
rows.anchor: bu nimete intihâbı da bir tesadüf değil, bile bile onlara bahşetmiş olduğu bazı meziyetler ve nimetler hasebiyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people called these ones are the Meccan unbelievers, who deny any life after the first death and reject resurrection.
rows.anchor: Şunlar: yani şu Mekke kâfirleri

words: أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍۢ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are challenged to compare themselves with Tubba's people and earlier nations, whom God destroyed for their sins.
rows.anchor: Ya onlar mı hayırlı yoksa Tübba‘ın kavmi ve ondan evvelkiler mi?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reply is that an individual's death is followed by the destruction of their people and nation, which is itself another death.
rows.anchor: Bunda iki suretle cevap vardır: Birinci ilk ölüm olan ferdin ölümünden sonra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reply proves resurrection from the need for just recompense and punishment; later verses explain this proof further.
rows.anchor: hakk u adl için cezânın lüzûmuna mebnî

rows.speaker: Ebû Ubeyde
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says Tubba was the title of every Yemeni king because people followed them; in pre-Islamic Arabia their rank resembled a caliph's and they were the greatest Arab kings.
rows.anchor: Yemen mülûkünün her birine ‘Tübba‘’ denilirdi, çünkü ehl-i dünya onlara tâbi‘olurlardı. Câhiliyede Tübba‘ın mevkii İslâm’da halifenin mevkii gibi idi

rows.speaker: Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha says Tubba himself was a righteous man.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe radıyallahu anhâ “Tübba‘bir recül-i sâlih idi” demiş

rows.speaker: Ka‘b
rows.claim: Ka'b says God condemned Tubba's people but did not condemn Tubba himself.
rows.anchor: Ka‘b da: “Allah teâlâ onun kavmini zemmetti, kendisini zemmetmedi” demiştir

rows.speaker: Kelbî
rows.claim: Kalbi identifies Tubba as Abu Karib As'ad.
rows.anchor: Kelbî “o, Ebû Kerb Es‘ad’dır” demiş

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says not to curse Tubba because he had become Muslim.
rows.anchor: Tübba‘a sebbetmeyin, çünkü o müslim

rows.speaker: Peygamber
rows.claim: Another report attributed to the Prophet says he did not know whether Tubba had been a prophet.
rows.anchor: Bilmem Tübba‘nebî midir değil midir?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, better means greater in strength and worldly might.
rows.anchor: daha kuvvetli ve şevketli mi
